app-fraud-triage.md.scenario: A retired Harborview customer is deceived by a bank-impersonation safe-account scam into an $18,650 instant payment whose beneficiary shows fan-in mule indicators.
fills: CASE_SUMMARY

Customer states: 'A man called saying he was from Harborview's fraud department. He gave a badge number and knew my name and the last four of my checking account. He said someone overseas was trying to drain my account and I had to move my money immediately into a protection account in my own name while they caught the person. He told me exactly what to type and said do not tell the branch because branch staff might be involved. He stayed on the line until the payment went through. About ninety minutes later I called the real number on my card and they told me nobody from the bank had called me.'
PAYMENT_DETAILS

Rail: RTP instant push payment (irreversible on settlement). Amount: $18,650.00 USD. Executed 2026-03-04 14:12 ET via the mobile app. Beneficiary name entered: 'Ridgeway Consulting LLC'. Beneficiary account 40027715 at Meridian Retail Bank (external). Payee status: NEW payee, added 2026-03-04 13:58 ET — about 14 minutes before the payment. Reference field: 'PROTECTION HOLD'. Customer first moved $19,000 from savings into checking at 13:56 ET to fund the transfer.
CUSTOMER_PROFILE

Margaret Halloran, age 68, retired schoolteacher, lives alone. Retail checking + savings, customer since 2004 (22-year tenure). Typical activity: monthly outflow around $2,800, card and bill payments; largest prior single payment on record $4,100. No prior fraud reports, no prior disputes. Vulnerability factors: age; sole account holder; reported she was frightened and acted under sustained phone pressure.
BENEFICIARY_INFO

Ridgeway Consulting LLC account 40027715 at Meridian Retail Bank opened 2026-01-28 (about 5 weeks before the payment). Per Meridian's preliminary recall response, the account received multiple inbound instant credits from unrelated remitters over the prior 6 days and dispersed them same-day, leaving little residual balance. Two other institutions have already lodged recall requests against the same account. Confirmation-of-Payee at add-time returned CLOSE MATCH / NOT EXACT.
WARNINGS_SERVED

In-app new-payee scam interstitial displayed at 14:03 ET: 'Have you been told to move money to a safe or protection account? Banks never ask this. This is a scam.' Session log shows the customer tapped 'I understand, continue'. Confirmation-of-Payee returned CLOSE MATCH / NOT EXACT for 'Ridgeway Consulting LLC' vs the registered account name. Login was by biometric on the customer's known device; no additional step-up or human callback was triggered. The customer says the caller told her to ignore any on-screen warning.
RECOVERABILITY

Payment executed 2026-03-04 14:12 ET; reported by the customer 2026-03-04 15:40 ET (about 90 minutes later). Recall request lodged with Meridian Retail Bank 2026-03-04 16:05 ET. Meridian's preliminary response 2026-03-05 09:00 ET indicates approximately $3,200 remains and is frozen pending the formal recall; the remainder was swept same-day. Recall window technically open but the majority of funds appear already dispersed.
PROVIDED_MATERIAL

Three items.
(1) Mobile-app session log (extract): 13:55 login OK (biometric), device 'MHalloran-iPhone', home IP; 13:56 internal transfer $19,000 savings to checking; 13:58 new payee 'Ridgeway Consulting LLC' acct 40027715 Meridian Retail Bank added, CoP returned CLOSE MATCH / NOT EXACT; 14:03 scam-warning interstitial shown, user tapped 'I understand, continue'; 14:12 RTP payment authorized $18,650.00 ref 'PROTECTION HOLD'; 15:40 inbound call from customer to card-servicing line, fraud reported.
(2) Customer written statement (taken by phone agent 2026-03-04): 'He said do not tell the branch. I was frightened. I moved everything from savings first, then sent it. He stayed on the line until it went through.'
(3) Meridian Retail Bank preliminary recall response (2026-03-05 09:00 ET): 'Beneficiary account opened 2026-01-28. Multiple inbound instant credits in the prior 6 days from unrelated remitters; funds largely dispersed same-day. Approximately $3,200 remains and is frozen pending your formal recall. Two other institutions have submitted recall requests against this account.'
PRIOR_OUTPUT
None — first review; baseline. No earlier triage or related disposition exists for this case.
scam type
Safe-account bank-impersonation APP scam, $18,650.00 USD, disposition Confirmed scam

fraud-typology-mapping.md.scenario: A Harborview fraud engineer maps the money-mule-network typology on retail instant payments into implementable detection-rule logic.
fills: NAMED_TYPOLOGY
Money mule network — receive-and-forward accounts funneling proceeds of authorized-push-payment scams to downstream collection accounts and crypto off-ramps
demand-deposit accounts
Retail demand-deposit accounts with real-time P2P and instant push payments (RTP) at Harborview Financial Group, including mobile-app self-service onboarding and instant external transfers
fields/tables

Available fields: transactions (txn_id, txn_amount, direction, channel, timestamp, counterparty_account, counterparty_bank), account (account_id, account_age_days, open_channel, declared_income, occupation_code), device/login (device_id, login_geo, ip_asn, session_id, biometric_flag), payee (payee_id, payee_age_days, payee_add_timestamp, cop_match_result), derived risk (inbound_sender_count_72h, outflow_ratio_sameday, residual_balance_min, velocity_out_24h). Not currently available: verified employer data, counterparty KYC at other banks, cross-institution scam-victim feed (external).
rules engine vs ML

Hybrid. A real-time rules engine sits on the payment-authorization path with a sub-300ms latency budget; a nightly batch behavioral layer scores accounts on aggregated 24h/72h features. Alerts route to a case-management queue with a fraud SAR/STR referral workflow. No production ML scoring yet — deterministic rules only.
analyst capacity

Approximately 1.4M active retail DDAs; instant-payment volume around 340,000 transactions/day. Fraud-analyst capacity roughly 120 alerts/day. Loss-tolerance target under 6 bps of instant-payment value. False-positive fatigue is the binding constraint — single-signal velocity rules previously ran near 85% false positive.
internal typology notes

Internal fraud-typology note 'Mule Networks — Instant Payments' (excerpt). Mule accounts laundering scam proceeds typically show: (a) account age under 90 days at first mule activity; (b) inbound from 5+ unrelated personal remitters within 72h; (c) same-day out-movement exceeding 90% of inbound, residual near zero (flow-through); (d) outbound concentrated to 1-3 collection accounts and/or a crypto off-ramp; (e) a shared device_id or ip_asn across multiple otherwise unrelated customer accounts (herder control); (f) inbound remitter names later surfacing in APP-scam victim reports. Loss vector: remitting victims bear the loss under authorized-push-payment scams; the mule DDA is the pass-through. Regulatory hook: fraud SAR/STR consideration on the mule account. Tuning history: single-signal (velocity alone) about 85% FP; multi-signal (velocity plus shared-device OR victim-report match) cut FP materially.
earlier version of this mapping
None — first mapping for this typology; baseline. No earlier rule set to refine or re-tune.

wire-fraud-disposition.md.scenario: A pending $247,900 commercial wire is flagged when a vendor's bank details change via an email from a lookalike domain.
fills: value date

$247,900.00 USD outbound wire (Fedwire), value date 2026-03-09. Originator: Cascadia Millwork LLC (Harborview commercial DDA 20 554 9013). Beneficiary: 'Timberline Supply Co.', account 8841200734 at Pacific Crest Bank, Portland OR (US domestic). Reference: invoice INV-2026-3391.
why it was flagged

Fraud rule WIRE-BEN-CHG-02: the beneficiary bank and account differ from all three most recent payments to this vendor, which routed to Willamette Trust, account ending 5567. Analyst note: the change-of-bank instruction arrived by email only and was marked urgent.
prior beneficiaries

Commercial account, tenure 8 years. Regular monthly vendor wires between $80,000 and $260,000. Established payee 'Timberline Supply Co.' with 11 prior wires over three years, all to Willamette Trust account ending 5567 (last on 2026-01-15). No prior fraud flags. Accounts payable is handled by a two-person finance team.
how the payment was instructed

The payment itself was instructed through the online banking portal by an authorized Cascadia AP user; the session was normal — known device and IP, MFA satisfied. The underlying bank-change instruction came as an emailed PDF titled 'updated remittance details' from ap-remit@timberline-supply.co. The vendor's prior legitimate correspondence used the domain timberlinesupply.com; this new mail uses timberline-supply.co (added hyphen, different top-level domain).
out-of-band (callback) verification

No out-of-band callback has been performed. The only phone number offered for confirmation is printed on the new emailed PDF itself (+1-503-555-0148). The vendor's known accounts-payable contact number on file, from the 2024 onboarding record, has not been called.
recall/return window

Status: pending — held in the wire-release queue, not yet transmitted. Same-day Fedwire cutoff is 17:00 ET; current time is 14:30 ET on 2026-03-09. Recall is not yet relevant because the item is unsent; the decision is hold vs. release.
email headers/thread

(1) Emailed 'updated remittance' (2026-03-08 16:41), From: 'Timberline Supply AP' <ap-remit@timberline-supply.co>, To: ap@cascadia-millwork.com, Subject: 'URGENT: updated banking for INV-2026-3391 — please action today'. Note: prior legitimate vendor mail used timberlinesupply.com; this uses timberline-supply.co.
(2) Invoice INV-2026-3391 (attached): $247,900.00, line items consistent with Timberline's usual millwork supply, but the layout differs slightly from prior invoices (logo position and font) and the remit-to bank block has been replaced.
